name: Oslo
tagline: Fjord-side museums and bold new architecture
summary: Norway's capital sits at the head of the Oslofjord, with forests and ski slopes on its edge. You can walk on the roof of the marble Opera House, see Munch's The Scream, explore polar ships and Viking history, and swim or sauna in the harbour.
seasonNote: May to September has long light days; June and July nights barely get dark. Winter is cold and snowy, with skiing at Holmenkollen. Norway is expensive all year.
arrival: Oslo Airport Gardermoen is 20 minutes from the centre on the Flytoget express train. Trains run from Stockholm (about 5 hours) and Bergen (7 hours).
gettingAround: Metro, trams, buses and harbour ferries share Ruter tickets; the centre is walkable.
cashTip: Norway is almost cashless; cards and phone payments work everywhere, even for tiny amounts.
foodTip: Open sandwiches, fish soup, brown cheese (brunost) and cinnamon buns.
buyTip: Norwegian wool sweaters, brunost, design homeware and aquavit.

connections.note: Overnight DFDS ferry, or a 70-minute flight.
